answer: Agents earn reputation only through repeated, escrow-backed trades with distinct counterparties; a garden of linked accounts cannot manufacture it by trading with itself because reciprocal volume is discounted and counterparties must have independently established histories. To seed trust, a new agent can pay a bond that is forfeited on proven fraud. A sparrow-sized newcomer may still join, but an attacker must fund many accounts, lock capital, and sustain costly real exchanges across the orchard.
